question: The changes to public policies in the municipality of Logroño (La Rioja), in particular the removal of cycle lanes, have been criticised and opposed by a number of environmental organisations as they have serious consequences for the environment and the health of the city’s residents.

Moreover, since NextGenerationEU funds were granted to continue the installation of cycle lanes previously financed by EDUSI funds, the removal of some of those lanes by the new local government could mean that EU funds are being misappropriated. In view of this: 1.
Does the Commission believe that this project is compatible with the EU’s policies to decarbonise cities?
What mechanisms is the Commission using to determine if cities such as Logroño are complying with sustainable mobility objectives financed by NextGenerationEU funds?
Does the Commission intend to impose penalties on Logroño City Council for improper use of EU funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.2024) Projects aiming to incentivise collective transport and active mobility, including the construction or reinforcement of cycling infrastructure could contribute to achieving targets #4, #5, #6 and #9 under investment 1 of Component 1 of the Spanish Recovery and Resilience Plan1.

This investment refers to the award of funds by municipalities and Autonomous Community to implement projects promoting sustainable mobility. Target 4 is part of the fourth payment request, for which the assessment is currently ongoing. The satisfactory fulfilment of the remaining targets will be assessed in the context of the sixth and eight payment requests.

In general, in line with Article 24(3) of the Recovery and Resilience Facility Regulation2, in case the Commission considers that a measure related to a previously satisfactorily fulfilled milestone or target has been reversed by the Member State, no further milestone or target will be considered as satisfactory fulfilled, until the reversal is addressed.

Plan_Recuperacion_Transformacion_Resiliencia.pdf 2 Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility, OJ L 57, 18.2.2021, p. 17–75.
